narrative.overview:
Desk reads like the departure board in a rail concourse. Every row keeps the same columns, every figure sits in its own cell, and status is said once, in a fixed place, in a colour that means one thing: amber is delayed, red is cancelled. On Desk the rows are the month’s entries ranked by date, amber marks an expense whose rate is still pending, and red marks a category over budget. When a pending rate arrives, the converted amount flips into place, once.

The world lends four things only: the palette (flap black and steel, letter white, delay amber, cancel red, one signal green for action), system mono figures in fixed cells with small spaced capitals for column heads, a board density, and the arrival flip. Layout, navigation and controls stay standard web ones: no icon tab bar, no brushed steel, no per-character flips.

Dark mode is the night board and the reference rendering; light mode is the daylight board. Surfaces lift at two heights, and motion is the flip plus feedback, dropping to zero under reduced motion. Proposed in ADR-0006; the Ledger Desk is the fallback.
keyCharacteristics: Entries as board rows with fixed columns and tabular amounts, in a real sortable table.
A row lamp: amber for a pending rate, red for an over-budget category, always with its word.
The departure tile: the remaining budget at Display size, the largest figure on the screen.
The arrival flip: a value that changes because data arrived turns over once.
Column heads and labels in small spaced capitals; reading text in mixed case.
Lifted surfaces at two heights, crisp 2/4/8px corners.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Green is the only accent: the primary action, the current location, spend.

rules.name: The Status Is Not a Series Rule
rules.body: Delay Amber and Cancel Red appear only as a row lamp, a status word, an over-budget fill or an error, never as a series, category or account colour.

rules.name: The Focus Is Blue Rule
rules.body: The focus ring is Focus Blue, 2px, with a 2px offset, on every interactive element in both themes.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every amount, rate and date is set in the figure face with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.

rules.name: The Fixed Columns Rule
rules.body: A column never moves or resizes when its values change.

rules.name: The Two Heights Rule
rules.body: Exactly two elevations, Raised and Overlay; board rows are flat inside a raised frame.

dos: Do keep columns fixed: values change, the board does not.
Do make the departure tile the largest figure on the screen, once.
Do say status twice, once as a lamp and once as a word.
Do flip a value only when new data arrives for it, once, under 280ms.
Do set every amount, rate and date in the figure face with tabular numerals.
Do keep column heads and labels in small spaced capitals and everything else in mixed case.
Do lift tiles and panels with Raised and use Overlay only above the page.
Do define colours as tokens in all three theme states.
donts: Don't add brushed steel, vent grids, flap textures, a split-flap font or per-character flips.
Don't use an icon tab bar or set inputs and buttons in flap cells.
Don't use amber or red for anything but delayed, pending, over budget or broken.
Don't add a chart library, a third shadow, a second accent or a second figure face.
Don't animate on load, on scroll, or a value the user did not cause to change.
Don't use green for focus; focus is always blue.
